Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can be used to predict a positive response to discography in patients with discogenic low back pain. A study found that HIZ (Hump Index of Spinal Stenosis) on MRI was predictive of positive results from discography.

However, it's essential to note that the overall accuracy and specificity of MRI for predicting concordant pain provocation during provocative disc injection may vary depending on individual patient factors, such as the presence of other conditions or the specific characteristics of the MRI scan. A more comprehensive analysis of multiple sub-questions would provide a clearer understanding of this topic.

In summary, while MRI can be useful in predicting positive results from discography in patients with discogenic low back pain, further research is needed to fully elucidate its accuracy and reliability for this specific purpose.
